beats.care: Into cybersecurity? Only test systems you own or have written permission for, like official bug bounty programmes. Curiosity is not a legal defence.
beats.what: Maharashtra Cyber says it stopped an attempted intrusion into its systems on Aug 15 and traced it via IP addresses to a 22-year-old student.
beats.why: The agency says hacking and unauthorised access are serious offences, and it wants to deter curious tech students.

opts: Probing a government server without permission
cards.q: According to Maharashtra Cyber, which of these can land you in legal trouble?
cards.why: The agency warned that unauthorised probing, testing or exploitation attempts on government systems can have legal consequences.

cards.body: He was called in and issued a notice. Reports do not mention an arrest or charges so far.
cards.caption: Age of the student questioned

cards.body: The agency's Security Operations Centre flagged odd activity. Investigators then followed the digital footprints and IP addresses back to the student.

hook: Is *just testing* a government website for bugs actually legal?

learn.t: Maharashtra Cyber says even unauthorised probing or testing of government websites and servers can bring legal consequences.

sources.name: Free Press Journal
sources.title: Maharashtra Cyber Foils Attempted Cyberattack On Its Digital Infrastructure, Questions 22-Year-Old Student

tldr: Maharashtra Cyber traced an attempted attack on its own systems to a 22-year-old college student and warned students that even 'testing' government sites can be illegal.
